images.title: Five pens at the counter
images.purpose: Open the chapter with a real purchase whose price has a decimal point, so students feel the need to multiply a decimal.
images.composition: A flat, simple shop counter fills the lower middle of the frame with 5 pens lying on it and one price tag; a small bill slip sits to the right; wide white space above.
exact_structure: A plain light grey #6B7280 counter top drawn as one long flat rectangle across the lower middle of the frame, outlined in #2B2B2B.
Exactly 5 identical pens lie side by side on the counter, evenly spaced, each a slim teal #0072B2 body with a grey #6B7280 tip and cap clip; no other pens anywhere.
One amber #E69F00 price tag on a string hangs from the leftmost pen, reading the text "₹9.5 each".
Under the row of pens, one short grey #6B7280 brace spans all 5 pens with the text "5 pens" centred below it.

To the right of the counter, one small white bill slip with a #2B2B2B outline, tilted slightly, carries two lines: "5 × ₹9.5" on the first line and "Total = ₹ ?" on the second line, the question mark in reddish purple #CC79A7.
No shopkeeper, no customer, no faces, no coins or notes, no other products; the top third of the frame is empty white space.
rejection: any count of pens other than exactly 5
the price shown as anything other than ₹9.5
people, faces or extra shop items cluttering the counter
images.takeaway: A real bill can need us to multiply a number that has a decimal point.
images.description: Five teal pens on a shop counter with a tag reading ₹9.5 each and a bill slip asking 5 × ₹9.5, Total = ₹ ?.
images.context: Shown beside the chapter opening text and the hook video, before any working.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to guess the total from the picture before anyone adds or multiplies.

image_decisions.why: The chapter opens with a purchase scene, and a picture of the 5 pens and the ₹9.5 price makes the question concrete before any working.
